turns.doctor_question: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response: Hi. Um, well, I came in because I keep getting stuck on this... this tiny uneven spot right around my nose and cheek. I just focus on it a lot, especially in photos or when I'm under the bright fluorescent lights at the store where I work. Even when other people tell me they don't really see it, it just feels like it's the very first thing the customers and my managers notice when they look at me.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient describes persistent focus and preoccupation with a perceived slight or unnoticeable flaw on their nose and cheek that others say they do not see.

turns.doctor_question: When you think about this spot on your nose and cheek, do you believe it's actually noticeable to other people, or do you recognize that it might not be as visible as it feels to you?
turns.patient_response: Um, I'm not really sure. Like, when my friends or my mom tell me they don't see it, I try to tell myself that maybe it isn't as bad as I think. But then... I don't know, when I'm actually looking at it in the mirror, it just looks so obvious to me. So I guess I kind of go back and forth on whether other people can actually see it or not.

turns.doctor_question: Besides looking in the mirror, do you find yourself doing other things repeatedly because of this spot—like picking at it, covering it up, or asking others if they notice it?
turns.patient_response:
Yeah, I do a few things. I don't really pick at it, but... when I'm on my breaks at work, I almost always end up checking my face in the bathroom mirror. I spend time fixing my hair around it, just trying to get it to fall right so it covers that spot. 

And I definitely compare myself to the girls who come through my checkout line at the store. I just look at them and notice how different they look compared to me. Sometimes I get so caught up in the bathroom checking and fixing my hair that I actually take way too long, and I end up being late getting back to the register.

symptom_reasoning.S068: The patient confirms engaging in repetitive behaviors related to appearance concerns, including frequent mirror checking, camouflaging the spot with hair, and comparing appearance to others.

turns.doctor_question: When you really think about it logically, do you recognize that your worry about this spot might be out of proportion to how noticeable it actually is, or does it genuinely seem as serious and noticeable as any other significant flaw would be?

turns.doctor_question: When you step back and think about it, do you recognize that you might be spending an unusual amount of time and energy worrying about this spot compared to how much most people would worry about a similar small mark on their face?

turns.doctor_question: Even though you just agreed that most people wouldn't spend this much time on it, when you're actually in that moment at work looking in the mirror, can you still recognize in that moment that you're probably overdoing it, or does it feel completely necessary and reasonable to you at that time?
